core_obligations: Set up the two index sets: I_n of six-tuples summing to n, whose monomials form a complement basis by the cited corollary, and J_n of seven-tuples with ijk = 0 and i+j+k+3ell+r+s+t = n, and observe that the obvious shift map J_n -> I_n is a bijection (proof lines 1674-1694).

Compare the two families modulo the previous layer: for a given element of J_n, the cited Omega-power lemma makes Delta_{n-1} contain the difference between the Omega form and q^{ell^2} times the monomial form, and the cited commutation lemma makes it contain the difference between that monomial and q^{2 j ell} times the shifted monomial (proof lines 1695-1712).

Conclude: combining the two congruences, each Omega-indexed element differs from a bijectively matched element of the known complement basis by an element of Delta_{n-1}, so the Omega-indexed family is again a basis for a complement of Delta_{n-1} in Delta_n (proof lines 1714-1720).
proof_roadmap: Match the new index set J_n bijectively with the index set I_n of the known complement basis (proof lines 1674-1694).
Use the Omega-power and commutation lemmas to move each Omega-indexed element to the matching monomial modulo Delta_{n-1}, and conclude by the known basis (proof lines 1695-1720).
difficulty_reason: The lemma exhibits a basis for a complement of the layer Delta_{n-1} inside Delta_n of the filtered algebra, namely the monomials in which the power of Omega appears instead of the compensated combination of A, B, C (statement lines 1658-1671). The proof compares the new family with the known monomial complement basis: it matches the two index sets by an explicit bijection, and then uses two cited lemmas to move each Omega-power element to the matching monomial modulo Delta_{n-1}, collecting the numerical factor q^{ell(2j+ell)} on the way (proof lines 1674-1712). The content is in the comparison, since the two families have different sizes of index sets and the bijection plus the two congruences are what transfer basisness; the final sentence then invokes the known complement basis. Both cited inputs are consumed inside the span, so H2.
